system_description.narrative_title: Energy chokepoints, AI arms race and competing blocs reshape a volatile order
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is in rapid flux as concurrent stressors—an Iran-driven Strait of Hormuz standoff and Russia‑Ukraine attacks on Black Sea logistics—disrupt energy and food flows while central banks and markets strain to absorb the shocks. Simultaneously an accelerated AI infrastructure buildout, financed by hyperscalers and Wall Street, is concentrating technological and economic leverage, even as alternative institutions (BRICS finance) and regional military moves deepen geopolitical fragmentation. These interacting processes create reinforcing feedbacks among energy markets, inflation/finance, and technology competition, producing systemic instability and opportunity.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, major corporations (tech hyperscalers, defence, energy), global commodity and capital markets, critical transit chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea), supply chains and AI infrastructure, and international institutions and finance mechanisms
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-technical system — the global civilization-scale order of states, markets, technology and transnational flows

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine armed conflict
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by domestic mobilization and Western military support, remain locked in a high-intensity war that is shifting battlefield control, degrading infrastructure and constraining Black Sea maritime routes.

variables.name: US–Iran maritime standoff and energy chokepoints
variables.description: The United States and Iran (and regional partners) are embroiled in a sustained naval and economic confrontation over control of the Strait of Hormuz and adjacent sea lanes, producing blockades, attacks on shipping and persistent oil‑market disruptions.

variables.name: US–China strategic tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are competing for long‑term strategic advantage across AI, semiconductors, supply chains and trade policy, using sanctions, investment controls and industrial subsidies to reshape technological leadership and economic leverage.

variables.name: Global bond markets and inflation repricing
variables.description: Global investors, central banks and major sovereign borrowers are confronting a bond‑market reckoning as shifting inflation, yields and monetary policy expectations reprice risk, constrain fiscal space and alter cross‑border capital flows.

variables.name: BRICS and Global‑South economic realignment
variables.description: BRICS members and other emerging economies are deepening financial, payments and trade cooperation to build alternatives to Western financial architectures and to blunt sanctions, shifting the contours of global economic governance.
